Water and health.question: 1) Safe and wholesome water should be free from:
Water and health.exp: Safe water should not contain disease-producing organisms. Freedom from pathogenic agents is a basic requirement. It prevents water-borne infections.

Water and health.question: 2) Safe drinking water should be free from harmful:
Water and health.exp: Wholesome water should not contain harmful chemicals. Chemical contamination may cause chronic toxicity. Examples include excess arsenic, fluoride and nitrate.

Water and health.question: 3) Pleasant water should be free from colour and:
Water and health.exp: Safe and wholesome water should be pleasant to taste. It should be free from colour and odour. Acceptability improves regular use.

Water and health.question: 4) Wholesome water should be usable for:
Water and health.exp: Wholesome water should be fit for household use. It should be safe, acceptable and usable. Domestic use includes drinking, cooking and washing.

Water and health.question: 5) Rainwater belongs to which category of water supply?
Water and health.exp: Rainwater is classified under rain. It is one of the main categories of water supply. Other broad groups are surface water and ground water.

Water and health.question: 6) Rivers and streams are examples of:
Water and health.exp: Rivers and streams are surface water. Tanks, ponds and lakes also belong to this group. Surface water is more easily contaminated.

Water and health.question: 7) Springs are examples of:
Water and health.exp: Springs are grouped under ground water. Shallow wells and deep wells are also ground water. Ground water is generally better protected than open surface water.

Water and health.question: 8) Tanks, ponds and lakes are examples of:
Water and health.exp: Tanks, ponds and lakes are surface water. They are open to environmental contamination. Treatment is needed before drinking.

Water and health.question: 9) Viral water-borne diseases include hepatitis A, hepatitis E and:
Water and health.exp: Viral water-borne diseases include hepatitis A, hepatitis E, poliomyelitis and rotavirus diarrhoea. They spread through contaminated water. Fecal contamination is an important route.

Water and health.question: 10) Rotavirus diarrhoea in infants is classified as:
Water and health.exp: Rotavirus is a viral cause of diarrhoea in infants. It can spread through contaminated water and poor hygiene. It is grouped under viral water-borne diseases.

Water and health.question: 11) Typhoid and paratyphoid fever are:
Water and health.exp: Typhoid and paratyphoid are bacterial infections. They are transmitted through contaminated water and food. Cholera and bacillary dysentery are also bacterial examples.

Water and health.question: 12) Cholera is classified as:
Water and health.exp: Cholera is a bacterial water-borne disease. It spreads through fecally contaminated water. Safe water and chlorination are important preventive measures.

Water and health.question: 13) Amoebiasis is a:
Water and health.exp: Amoebiasis is caused by protozoa. It is transmitted through contaminated water or food. Giardiasis is another protozoal example.

Water and health.question: 14) Giardiasis is caused by:
Water and health.exp: Giardiasis is a protozoal infection. It is transmitted by contaminated water. It can cause diarrhoea and malabsorption.

Water and health.question: 15) Roundworm and threadworm are examples of:
Water and health.exp: Roundworm and threadworm are helminths. They may be transmitted through contaminated environment and poor sanitation. Hydatid disease is also listed under helminthic infection.

Water and health.question: 16) Weil disease is caused by:
Water and health.exp: Weil disease is a leptospiral infection. It is related to contaminated water exposure. It may be associated with animal urine contamination.

Water and health.question: 17) Schistosomiasis is associated with which aquatic host?
Water and health.exp: Schistosomiasis is associated with snail as aquatic host. The life cycle involves freshwater snails. It is important in water-related disease transmission.

Water and health.question: 18) Guinea worm disease is associated with:
Water and health.exp: Guinea worm disease is associated with Cyclops. Cyclops acts as an aquatic host. Fish tapeworm is also listed with Cyclops.

Water and health.question: 19) Fish tapeworm is associated with:
Water and health.exp: Fish tapeworm is listed with Cyclops as aquatic host. This is a water-related parasitic transmission point. It is different from schistosomiasis, which involves snail.

Water and health.question: 20) The WHO limit for arsenic in drinking water is:
Water and health.exp: WHO limit for arsenic is ≤0.01 mg/L. Bangladesh value mentioned separately is 0.05 mg/L. Arsenic is a major chemical hazard in drinking water.

Water and health.question: 21) The Bangladesh value mentioned for arsenic is:
Water and health.exp: Bangladesh value for arsenic is mentioned as 0.05 mg/L. WHO limit is lower at 0.01 mg/L. Arsenic contamination is an important public health issue.

Water and health.question: 22) The drinking water limit for fluoride mentioned is:
Water and health.exp: Fluoride limit is mentioned as ≤1.0 mg/L. Excess fluoride may cause fluorosis. Both deficiency and excess have public health importance.

Water and health.question: 23) The drinking water limit for nitrate mentioned is:
Water and health.exp: Nitrate limit is mentioned as ≤50 mg/L. High nitrate in drinking water is dangerous especially for infants. It may lead to methemoglobinemia.

Water and health.question: 24) Fecal coliform count allowed in drinking water should be:
Water and health.exp: Fecal coliforms should be absent in drinking water. The standard mentioned is 0 per 100 mL. Any fecal coliform suggests fecal contamination.

Water and health.question: 25) Gold standard indicator for fecal contamination of water is:
Water and health.exp: E. coli or fecal coliform count indicates fecal contamination. It is considered the gold standard indicator. It reflects possible presence of enteric pathogens.

Water and health.question: 26) The primary method of preventing water-borne diseases mentioned is:
Water and health.exp: Chlorination is mentioned as the primary method of preventing water-borne diseases. It disinfects water by killing many pathogens. It is widely used for public water supply.

Water and health.question: 27) High nitrate in drinking water is classically associated with:
Water and health.exp: Nitrate can be reduced to nitrite in infants. Nitrite converts hemoglobin to methemoglobin, reducing oxygen carriage. This produces “blue baby syndrome.” Infants are more vulnerable due to gastric and enzymatic factors.

Water and health.question: 28) Excess fluoride in drinking water may cause:
Water and health.exp: Excess fluoride causes dental and skeletal fluorosis. Dental fluorosis causes mottling of teeth. Skeletal fluorosis may cause bone and joint problems. Control of fluoride level is important because both low and high fluoride are harmful.

Water and health.question: 29) Chronic arsenic exposure through drinking water may cause:
Water and health.exp: Chronic arsenic exposure causes skin pigmentation and keratosis. Long-term exposure increases cancer risk. The problem is classically linked with contaminated tube-well water in affected regions. Prevention depends on safe alternative water and monitoring.

Water and health.question: 30) The most reliable way to make household water microbiologically safe during emergency is:
Water and health.exp: Boiling kills most pathogenic organisms when done properly. It is useful at household level during outbreaks or emergencies. The water should be stored safely after boiling to prevent recontamination. Boiling does not remove chemical toxins like arsenic.

Water and health.question: 31) Slow sand filter mainly acts through a biological layer called:
Water and health.exp: Slow sand filtration depends greatly on a biological layer on the sand surface. This layer is called schmutzdecke or vital layer. It helps remove microorganisms and organic matter. The filter becomes more effective after this layer matures.

Water and health.question: 32) Alum is commonly used in water treatment for:
Water and health.exp: Alum is used as a coagulant. It helps suspended particles form flocs. These flocs settle more easily during sedimentation. Coagulation improves clarity and later filtration efficiency.

Water and health.question: 33) Chlorination is least effective against:
Water and health.option3: Protozoal cysts compared with many bacteria
Water and health.exp: Chlorination is very useful against many bacteria and viruses. However, some protozoal cysts are relatively resistant. Filtration plus disinfection gives better protection. This is why clear water and proper treatment sequence matter.

Water and health.question: 34) Free residual chlorine after adequate contact time indicates:
Water and health.exp: Residual chlorine means some chlorine remains after disinfection. It gives continued protection during distribution. Adequate contact time is needed before judging effectiveness. Residual chlorine does not remove chemical contaminants like arsenic.

Water and health.question: 35) The usual sequence in municipal water purification is:
Water and health.exp: Public water treatment usually includes storage, filtration and chlorination before distribution. Storage allows natural purification and settling. Filtration removes suspended matter and many organisms. Chlorination provides final disinfection.

Water and health.question: 36) A sanitary well should preferably be protected by:
Water and health.option2: Parapet, platform and drainage away from well
Water and health.exp: A sanitary well should prevent contamination from surface runoff. A raised parapet and pucca platform help protect the opening. Wastewater should drain away from the well. Nearby latrines or stagnant drains increase fecal contamination risk.

Water and health.question: 37) Turbidity in water mainly interferes with:
Water and health.exp: Turbid water contains suspended particles. Microorganisms may be protected inside these particles. Chlorination works better in clear water. Therefore, sedimentation and filtration before disinfection are important.

Water and health.question: 38) Water hardness is mainly due to salts of:
Water and health.exp: Hardness of water is mainly due to calcium and magnesium salts. Temporary hardness is usually due to bicarbonates. Permanent hardness is due to sulphates, chlorides and nitrates. Hard water causes scaling and increased soap consumption.

Water and health.question: 39) Residual chlorine in drinking water is commonly checked by:
Water and health.exp: Orthotolidine test is used to detect residual chlorine. It gives a colour change when chlorine is present. This helps monitor whether chlorination has been adequate. Regular testing is important in treated water supplies.

Water and health.question: 40) The best prevention of water-borne disease at community level is:
Water and health.option1: Safe water supply with sanitation and hygiene
Water and health.exp: Water-borne diseases are prevented by safe water, sanitation and hygiene together. Treatment of cases alone cannot stop transmission. Safe disposal of feces prevents water contamination. Handwashing and food hygiene add further protection.
